subject: Capacity skyline, credit structure and ops ask for renewal
body:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@skylarklabs.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity skyline, credit structure and ops ask for renewal

Hi Adeel —

Quick follow from our renewal planning notes. We pulled a short ops/KPI snapshot for Skylark covering the last 6 months and a set of microbenchmarks (latency and token cost by model variant) that matter for the next term. High-level we see: 

- Current run-rate (30d MA): ~120M tokens/month (mostly embedding+chat mix)
- Projected growth if new NLU pipeline ships (Q4): base case 190–220M tokens/month; high case ~320M
- Latency profile: p95 generation for chat-md small model is stable at 220ms; p95 for larger mixed requests increases linearly with seq length (we included per-variant numbers in the microbenchmarks).

Ask: can you confirm the Q4 product rollout window and whether the forecast below is realistic from your end? If so, we want to propose a capacity skyline + credit structure rather than a single flat commit:

Proposed structure (draft):
- Tier A (Base commit): 150M tokens/month at current rate card (12-month term)
- Tier B (Surge buffer): option to purchase 100M tokens/month at 20% discounted rate; exercised monthly with 14-day notice
- One-time onboarding credit to offset migration/do-up costs: $12k applied to first invoice
- 60-day pilot of Dedicated burst lane during heavy jobs (priority routing; usage metered separately)

I attached: skylark_usage_snapshot_q3.pdf (usage breakdown, cadence heatmap), rlm_token_mix_microbenchmarks.csv (per-model token cost and latency), and a renewal_credit_table_v2.xlsx (worked examples).

If that all looks directionally right, can we schedule a 30-min sync the week of Sep 20 to lock the deal structure? Grace/Ben/Karthik are cc'd to help with the pilot logistics, credit mechanics, and pricing sensitivity.

Thanks —
Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143


-----Original Message-----
From: Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@skylarklabs.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@skylarklabs.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Capacity skyline, credit structure and ops ask for renewal

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the note and the attachments. Quick answers from our side: 

- Product rollout: we are targeting internal beta Nov 8, public rollout Dec 15. So Q4 acceleration is accurate.
- Usage forecast: the base/high splits you show line up with our internal model (we had 200M base / 300M high).
- Dedicated pilot: yes please — would be good to validate latency under production traffic and the prefetching behavior you mentioned earlier.

A couple of asks from our Ops/Finance team before we sign: 
1) Clear invoice cadence for the surge buffer (monthly true-up vs. pre-purchase).
2) Banding on preemptible vs. reserved compute in the Dedicated pilot (we need an SLA on minimum throughput for the pilot window).
3) Evidence of audit logs and data residency controls for burst lane traffic (SOC2 artifact pointer would be helpful).

Happy to take a 30-min call next Tue (Sep 21) after 2pm PT — Lisa is looping in our finance lead if we get to pricing mechanics.

—Adeel

Adeel Khan
Head of Platform
Skylark Labs
adeel.khan@skylarklabs.com

>

> Agenda (30 min):

> - Walk renewal structure options and worked examples (attached sheet)
> - Pilot definition: Dedicated burst SLA and data handling checklist
> - Next steps and contracting timeline (DocuSign target if we agree)
>

> 
> Grace / Ben / Karthik — can you review the credit table and microbenchmarks, and confirm whether the proposed onboarding credit and surge discount are within typical guardrails?
> 
> Thanks — J

--
Jasmine Liu


-----Reply from Grace O'Connor (internal)-----
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@skylarklabs.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity skyline, credit structure and ops ask for renewal

Thanks J — looked through the snapshot. A few operational clarifications we should finalize on the call: 

- Pilot SLA: propose 99.5% availability for Dedicated burst lane over the 60-day window with an ops contact and runbook. We'll log incidents into the shared Jira project (link in the sheet).
- Audit evidence: I'll attach SOC2 artifact pointers to the meeting invite; we can also provide sample audit logs filtered for the pilot traffic.
- Prefetch behavior: ops will enable KV prefetch for the first 4 weeks and then switch to real-time prefetch to validate cache hit delta. We'll capture token delta metrics during that time.

I'll prepare a short pilot runbook and add it to the drive link in the calendar invite.

—Grace

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com


-----Reply from Ben Carter (internal)-----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@skylarklabs.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity skyline, credit structure and ops ask for renewal

Quick pricing note: the onboarding credit at $12k is fine from a deal-econ perspective. Two items we should account for in the final paperwork: 

1) If Skylark exercises >80% of the surge buffer for two consecutive months, propose an automatic rate-lock on Tier B for the remainder of the term (protects both sides).
2) If the Dedicated pilot shows >15% reduction in per-token cost due to caching/batching, offer a one-time invoice credit equal to 10% of the measured savings (so they capture upside).

I'll draft the language for those bullets and drop into the shared renewal_credit_table_v2.xlsx — tagging Karthik for legal/contract wording.

—Ben


-----Final confirmation from Karthik Iyer (internal)-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Adeel Khan <adeel.khan@skylarklabs.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity skyline, credit structure and ops ask for renewal

Confirmed — the structure and the conditional language Ben proposed look good. A couple of legal/finance clarifications before DocuSign: 

- Surge buffer mechanics: default to monthly true-up (we invoice for surge usage at the end of the month). If Skylark prefers pre-purchase we can convert to a committed tranche but that requires a minimum 6-month term on the tranche.
- Rate-lock clause: we'll add explicit measurement windows and a cap on the number of automatic adjustments (max one rate-lock per 12-month term).
- SLA for pilot: legal wants the pilot SLA to be scoped to availability and throughput for the burst lane only, not the entire account. We'll put a 30-day termination right for Redwood if pilot traffic (malicious/unexpected) exceeds agreed thresholds.

Adeel — I'll push an updated commercial term sheet and proposed contract language later today. If the pilot/runbook and the usage forecast look good, DocuSign target still Sep 28.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Commercial Ops
karthik.iyer@redwood.com


Attachments referenced: skylark_usage_snapshot_q3.pdf, rlm_token_mix_microbenchmarks.csv, renewal_credit_table_v2.xlsx

Action items summary:
- Adeel: share month-by-month forecast (Nov–Mar) before Tue 9/21 call (Adeel said finance lead will join).
- Grace: add SOC2 pointers & pilot runbook to calendar invite.
- Ben/Karthik: finalize conditional credit & rate-lock language and update the credit spreadsheet.
- Jasmine: schedule 30-min sync for Tue 9/21 2:30pm PT and circulate DocuSign draft on Sep 24 if terms align.
